transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I keep having these awful thoughts I can’t shake, like that I’ve missed something critical. It sounds small when I say it out loud, but it doesn’t feel small. I work with numbers, and I’ll get stuck on the idea that maybe there was one wrong number in a data release, or I sent out something with an error that could cause a big problem. And then it spreads to other things too, like whether the back door is really locked, or whether I paid a bill from the wrong account.

Even when I know I checked it — sometimes I can remember checking it — my mind keeps saying, “But what if you didn’t? What if you’re remembering wrong? What if this causes a disaster and it’s your fault?” It just won’t let go of the possibility. That’s really why I’m here. It’s gotten to where I feel like I can’t trust my own checking or my own memory.
When you have these thoughts, do you find yourself doing certain things over and over, like checking, counting, or repeating actions, even if you know they don’t make sense?

Yes. I do. I mean, I know it’s excessive, and even while I’m doing it there’s this part of me that’s saying, “You already checked this,” but I can’t seem to stop at just once.

With work, I’ll reopen the same spreadsheet again and again, sometimes after I’ve already closed it and told myself I was done. I’ll go back through columns, formulas, totals, the released numbers — and then if I notice I skimmed something too quickly, I feel like I have to start that section over. Emails are the same way. I reread them line by line, especially if there’s an attachment or a number in them, because I’m afraid I missed one detail that changes everything.

And it isn’t just work. I’ll check the locks in a certain order, like back door, front door, windows, then back door again, and if I don’t feel certain enough, I repeat it. Payment confirmations too — I’ll pull up the account, check the amount, check who it went to, check the date, and then somehow still feel like I might have paid it wrong.

It’s not that it makes sense exactly. It’s more like I’m trying to get to this feeling of “safe” or “settled,” and if I don’t get that feeling, I keep going. Some nights I’m still sitting at my desk hours later, opening the same things over and over, and the awful part is I haven’t actually finished anything. I’m just… stuck checking.
Do these thoughts and checking behaviors cause you a lot of distress, or make it hard for you to get through your day, like affecting your work or relationships?

Yes, very much. It’s not just annoying or time-consuming anymore — it’s really interfering.

At work, I’ve fallen behind on major deadlines because I stay late reviewing things. I’ll think, “Okay, I’ll just do one more pass,” but one pass turns into another and then another, and somehow hours are gone. The awful thing is I’m not even necessarily producing better work at that point. I’m just stuck trying to feel certain enough, and then I still don’t finish what I was supposed to finish. So I end up behind, and then the pressure makes the checking even worse.

And outside of work, I’ve started missing things I actually used to look forward to. I used to go to salsa nights, and I liked kayaking too — those were things that helped me feel like I had a life outside of spreadsheets and obligations. But now I’ll plan to go, and then I can’t get away from the checking or the reviewing in time. I’ll tell myself I’ll leave after I verify one last thing, and then suddenly it’s too late, or I’m too exhausted, or I feel like I can’t leave until I’m sure.

So yes, it causes a lot of distress. It feels like my day gets swallowed up by trying to make sure nothing is wrong.

Do you ever experience intrusive, unwanted thoughts that are more disturbing or violent in nature, such as thoughts about harming someone, or having inappropriate sexual thoughts, even if you would never act on them?

Not really in the sense of wanting to hurt someone, or sexual thoughts like that. The intrusive thoughts I get are more… they’re disturbing because they feel catastrophic, if that makes sense.

It’s like this awful thought that I’ve missed something critical — a wrong number in a data release, or the back door wasn’t actually locked, or I paid a bill from the wrong account — and then my mind grabs onto it and won’t let go. Even if I know I checked it, even if I can picture myself checking it, there’s still this voice saying, “But what if you’re wrong? What if this causes a disaster and it’s your fault?”

So no, it’s not that I’m imagining harming someone. It’s more that I’m terrified I’ve already made some mistake that could hurt people or create a huge problem, and I just don’t know it yet.
